title: The Real Reason You See Lights Chasing Each Other
hook: Your brain invents movement that isn't there.

narration.text: Your brain invents movement that isn't there.
This is called apparent motion, a visual illusion.
When lights flash sequentially, your brain fills the gaps.
It creates a perception of continuous movement between them.
You can test this with traffic lights at night.
Notice how the red, amber, and green lights appear to chase.
Try it right now, and tell me if it worked on you.
Like this if it surprised you, and subscribe for more mind-bending facts.

description: Ever wonder why traffic lights seem to chase each other? It's not magic, it's your brain playing tricks on you. This short explains the fascinating visual illusion of apparent motion.
topic: Why you often perceive moving lights as if they are chasing each other, even if they are not. This is a visual illusion you can test with traffic lights.
